problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{3}-\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{2}=1.$

activity_context.topic_title: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at a General Point

feedback.problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{25}-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{9}=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a vertical hyperbola, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{a}{b}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
a=\sqrt{25}=5,\,b=\sqrt{9}=3,\,h=2,\,k=2.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes are given by

$$
y-2=\pm \frac{5}{3}(x-2).
$$
